principle: Scores are evidence, not the edit. They rank the legal choices for a boundary; they do not choose. hold_a is always offered and must always be weighed by the editor.
recommended_by_score_is: informational only — not the creative answer

duration_choice_rules.b_early: anticipate the boundary by one beat, carrying this event's own B_ACTION length (its action peak lands ON the boundary)
duration_choice_rules.b_glance: brief useful detail — exit on the first BEAT at/after the strongest visible movement in the slot
duration_choice_rules.b_action: hold through the visible action — exit on the first BEAT at/after the end of the contiguous action run around that peak
duration_choice_rules.b_hold: continue past the action to the next useful musical boundary — exit on the first DOWNBEAT at/after the action run end
duration_choice_rules.endpoint_provenance: every endpoint is a beat or downbeat of the same beat/phrase artifact the cut grid uses; every length is clamped to minimum_b_shot, maximum_b_shot and the remaining slot width, and the clamp that fired is recorded per candidate
